review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the simp-relevant dependencies: Padic.natCard_residueField (@[simp high]), abelianizedLocalCyclotomicCharacter_mk (@[simp]), cyclotomicCharacter_absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv (@[simp]), and the private padicPrimeUnit in ExplicitCyclotomicSymbol/Basic.lean. The file declares no simp lemmas and no simp-set conflicts or loops are visible. I found only one weak interface issue: the prime `p` as a unit of ℚ_[p] has no canonical public name or simp API. I did not run Lean, so how the simp calls behave is uncertain. In particular, `localArtinMap_Q2_zeta5` uses `simpa using hσ` to match a numeral-cast unit, and I could not check how fragile that is.

findings.problem: The uniformizer `p ∈ ℚ_[p]ˣ` is spelled out as `Units.mk0 (p : ℚ_[p]) (Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 ...)` in the hypotheses of four public theorems and in two private proofs. Another file already has the canonical term as a private definition, `padicPrimeUnit`, but it is not exported. So there is no shared normal form and no simp lemmas for it, such as `Units.val` and valuation facts. As a result, `localArtinMap_Q2_zeta5` has to bridge `Units.mk0 (2:ℚ_[2])` and `Units.mk0 ((2:ℕ):ℚ_[2])` with `simpa using hσ`. That relies on simp rewriting the cast inside a term with a dependent proof argument. Statements built from different spellings of this unit will not match syntactically.
findings.proposed_change: Move `padicPrimeUnit p : ℚ_[p]ˣ` out of ExplicitCyclotomicSymbol/Basic.lean into a public location, for example the Padic local-field file. Add `@[simp] coe_padicPrimeUnit : (padicPrimeUnit p : ℚ_[p]) = p`. State the hypotheses of the theorems in this file with `padicPrimeUnit p`. Then `localArtinMap_Q2_zeta5` only needs a `Nat.cast_ofNat`-style bridge, stated once, in place of the `simpa` over a dependent `mk0`.
findings.benefit: The hypotheses become short and uniform. Different files stop restating the unit in slightly different forms (`Units.mk0 (p : ℚ_[p]) hp0`, `set π := ...`). Simp then has one canonical form to normalize to, so downstream rewrites and `exact` applications of these theorems match without ad hoc `simpa`.
